subject: Regional redundancy & pricing options for multi-region Dedicated commit
messages:
From: Olivia Zhang <olivia@orbitai.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah@redwood.com>
Cc: Samuel Reed <s.reed@finpay.io>
Date: Wed, 7 Apr 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Multi-region Dedicated ask — sizing, replication, and discount bands

Hi Hannah,

Thanks for the demo last week — OrbitAI is close to selecting a Dedicated provider. Before we proceed to procurement we need a clear pricing and packaging proposal that covers multi-region requirements. High level: 

- Primary: US (west) pool with steady-state 64 A100-equivalent GPUs, burst to 96 for traffic spikes.
- Secondary: EU (Frankfurt) pool with steady-state 24 GPUs, burst to 48 — used for regional serving and DR.
- Requirements: 99.9% availability per region, <120ms p95 for 8k-context generation under small-batch realtime traffic.
- Cross-region routing: prefer smart routing (latency-first) with automatic failover to secondary if primary capacity constrained.
- Replication/DR: synchronous KV-cache replication is optional — preferred approach is fast failover plus model variant fallback.

Procurement questions: pricing tiers for 1yr vs 3yr reserved commits, incremental discount waterfall for larger commits, whether we can carve out dedicated pools per region under one contract, and if you offer cross-region replication add-ons (and their unit pricing).

Can you sketch three options (standard, performance, and enterprise) with expected monthly committed spend ranges and indicative discounts? Also send any procurement-friendly artifacts (SOW template, pricing sheet, and typical SLA language). We need something to show legal and finance by next Wednesday.

Thanks,
Olivia
Director of Platform
OrbitAI

Olivia — thanks, that’s clear and very helpful. I’ll outline options and include a pricing workbook for you to hand to finance. Quick clarifying Qs before we put numbers: 

1) Is the 64 A100-equivalent steady-state the committed reserve you want in US-west, or is that expected peak steady state with a separate reserve ask?
2) Do you expect KV-cache replication to be required for cold-starts or only for warm-session transfer during failover?
3) Any compliance constraints for EU writes (data residency)?

I’m looping Marissa (pricing) and Dev (solutions) to draft the three-tier options and SOW language. We’ll aim to send an initial workbook today and an updated SOW by EOD tomorrow.

—Hannah

From: Olivia Zhang <olivia@orbitai.com>

Date: Wed, 7 Apr 2027 11:18:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Multi-region Dedicated ask — sizing, replication, and discount bands

Thanks, Hannah. Answers inline: 

1) The 64 in US-west should be the committed reserve (we want predictable unit economics). Peak bursts to 96 are expected but not committed.
2) KV replication is optional — we prefer fast failover and model-variant fallback to avoid synchronous cross-region writes. If you have a lightweight incremental replication add-on we’d like to see the cost.
3) EU writes must remain in-region for EU customer data; routing should respect data residency when a region-originated request contains EU-resident data.

If you can give a 1yr vs 3yr dollar commitment and effective % discounts per tier, that’ll help. Also want to understand change windows (how easy to move reserved GPUs between pools over the term).

Olivia

Subject: Re: Multi-region Dedicated ask — pricing options & SOW

Hi Olivia — appreciate the speedy clarification. Attached is a preliminary workbook (Redwood_Dedicated_MultiRegion_Pricing_0427.xlsx) and a draft SOW we can adapt. Summary of three options below (numbers are indicative ranges; detailed line-item sheet attached):

- Standard: Committed reserve = US-west 48 GPUs, EU 24 GPUs. 1yr term. Baseline throughput SLA 99.5% per region. Pricing: mid-range per-GPU rate, no replication add-ons. Estimated monthly commit: $X1 — $X2.

- Performance: Committed reserve = US-west 64 GPUs (matches your ask), EU 24 GPUs. 1yr term (3yr option available). 99.9% SLA, prioritized scheduling for bursts up to 1.5x. Pricing: ~10–18% discount vs on-demand depending on term. Monthly commit: $Y1 — $Y2. Includes options for cross-region routing policy and warm-cache support (incremental replication add-on quoted separately).

- Enterprise: Committed reserve = US-west 64 GPUs, EU 48 GPUs, 3yr term. 99.95% SLA and guaranteed <120ms p95 for configured workload (subject to traffic profile). Pricing: larger waterfall discounts (18–30% effective). Includes optional DR replication (asynchronous KV snapshotting) and priority engineering SLA for runbook/DR tests.

Replication add-on options: lightweight async replication (periodic KV snapshots for faster cold-starts) or warm-cache sync for per-request low-latency continuity. We’ve provided per-GPU-month pricing and a flat monthly fee for cross-region replication control plane in the workbook.

Doc notes: change windows — we support reallocation of reserved units between pools on a quarterly cadence with modest admin fees; immediate intra-term reassignments can be accommodated for larger commits with a pro-rated adjustment.

I’ll follow up with line-item dollar ranges in a separate sheet (sending now). If you’re comfortable, we can prepare SOW_draft_v1.pdf for legal review and a DocuSign envelope for signature.

—Marissa

Hi Olivia/Samuel — following up with the requested clarifications. Please see the attached workbook for line-item dollars; highlights here: 

- Committed billing model: single contract + single invoice covering all regional pools. We provide a per-region allocation table for accounting so you can treat pools as separate ledger items.
- Bursting: bursts beyond committed reserve billed at a discounted on-demand uplift; for 1yr commits uplift is ~30% above committed unit price; for 3yr commits uplift is ~20%. We can create a monthly credit accrual if you consistently under-utilize commit (this is negotiable for deals > $2M ARR).
- Data residency: EU writes stay within EU; routing policy enforces origin-aware routing where EU origin requests are routed to EU pool. Replication add-on does not move EU resident writes out-of-region.
- Change windows: quarter-to-quarter reassignment of reserved units, same-term reassignments possible with pro-rate and change fee for 1yr deals; for 3yr we offer two free reassignments.

Next steps: if the workbook looks good we’ll prepare the SOW_draft_v1.pdf and a DocuSign envelope. Suggest a call Monday to lock on final numbers and any enterprise-specific legal language.

Best,
Avery Johnson
Director, Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference
